title: Candidate moves: list and prune

D0.outcome: Explains why moves are listed before they are analysed and why a candidate is dropped only for a concrete reason.

D1.outcome: Writes a list of two to four candidates for a given position, starting with the forcing moves and including one quiet move, each with a one-line purpose.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, produces a list that contains the best move in at least 8 of 10, with no more than four moves.

D3.outcome: Prunes a list to one move by naming a concrete refutation for each dropped candidate, and notices when a new candidate appears only after the first move is played.

misconceptions: The first move that comes to mind is the candidate and the rest is padding.
A move is dropped because it looks bad, not because a refutation was found.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map)
docs/council-synthesis.md Round 3 and CD-3 (candidate lists, analysis tree)
sources/sheets/emlasker_common-sense.md §4.11 (three kinds of move) and §4.13 (plans rather than trees)
conditions: Not a forced position; more than one plan is plausible.
Forcing moves are listed first; quiet moves are included because positional moves are neither threats nor parries.
contrasts: A list of near-duplicates (the same idea in two move orders).
Dropping a candidate by feel and later finding it was the only move.
A forced reply to a check, where there is nothing to list.
